<thought>To determine the number of carbonyl (C=O) groups, I will first obtain the 13C NMR spectrum of the compound using the `carbon_nmr_spectra` tool. Carbonyl carbons typically appear downfield (≈190–220 ppm). After retrieving the spectrum, I will compare the observed peaks with the typical carbonyl chemical shift range (using `retrieve_carbon_shifts`) and count how many peaks fall within that range. This will give the number of C=O groups without needing additional costly experiments.</thought>
